G01.title: "is / am / are" (polite)
G01.expl: Put 이에요 after a noun ending in a consonant, 예요 after a vowel. It works for I, you, he, she, it and they. Make it a question just by raising your voice: 이에요?

cloze.en: I'm a student.

G02.title: topic marker: "as for…"
G02.expl: 은/는 marks what you are talking about. Use 은 after a consonant, 는 after a vowel. It often shows contrast: "As for me…".

cloze.en: I'm Jamie.

G03.title: subject marker
G03.expl: 이/가 points at the subject, especially new information or the answer to "who / what". 이 after a consonant, 가 after a vowel. Question words take it: 누가 (who), 뭐가 (what).

cloze.en: Where is the bathroom?

G04.title: "is not"
G04.expl: To say something is NOT a noun, use N이/가 + 아니에요.

cloze.en: That isn't the bathroom.

G05.title: "there is / there isn't", "is located at"
G05.expl: 있어요 = there is, (I) have, is (at a place). 없어요 = there isn't, don't have. 에 marks the place: 방에 있어요 = it's in the room.
ex: to be (somewhere), there is, to have
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
There's no window in the room.
to not be, there isn't, to not have

cloze.en: The bathroom is on this floor.

G06.title: possessive "'s", "my"
G06.expl: 의 works like "'s": 할머니의 집 = Grandma's house. In speech it is often dropped: 할머니 집. "My" is 제 (polite) or 내 (casual).
ex: This is my younger sibling's photo.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: My name is Jamie.

G07.title: 일, 이, 삼… for phone numbers, years, money, room numbers
G07.expl: Korean has two number sets. These (일 이 삼 사 오 육 칠 팔 구 십, 백, 천, 만) are used for phone numbers, dates, money, minutes and room numbers. 11 is 십일, 20 is 이십.

cloze.en: My room is number 3.

G08.title: "also, too"
G08.expl: 도 replaces 은/는 or 이/가 and means "too". 저도 = me too.

cloze.en: I'm American too.

G09.title: "and, with"
G09.expl: 하고 and (이)랑 join nouns ("A and B") or mean "with". (이)랑 is a bit more casual; use 이랑 after a consonant.
ex: I have a mom and a dad.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
I live with my younger sibling.

cloze.en: I have an older brother and an older sister.

G10.title: present tense, polite
G10.expl: Take the verb's dictionary form (먹다), drop 다 (먹), then: if the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ add 아요 (가요, 와요); otherwise add 어요 (먹어요). 하다 becomes 해요. Vowels often merge: 가 + 아요 = 가요, 마시 + 어요 = 마셔요.

cloze.en: I eat kimchi.

G11.title: object marker
G11.expl: 을/를 marks the thing you do something to. 을 after a consonant, 를 after a vowel. In casual speech it's often dropped.

cloze.en: I drink coffee.

G12.title: "don't, doesn't"
G12.expl: Put 안 in front of a verb to make it negative: 안 먹어요. For 하다 verbs, 안 goes before 하다: 공부 안 해요. -지 않아요 means the same and sounds a little more formal.

cloze.en: I don't drink alcohol.

G13.title: "I want to…"
G13.expl: Verb stem + 고 싶어요 = want to do. Ask with 뭐 먹고 싶어요? = What do you want to eat?
ex: What do you want to drink?

cloze.en: I want to make kimchi.

G14.title: polite request, "please…"
G14.expl: Verb stem + 세요 (after a vowel) or 으세요 (after a consonant) is a polite way to ask someone to do something. Some verbs have special forms: 먹다 → 드세요 (please eat).

cloze.en: Please have some of this.

G15.title: "please give me…"
G15.expl: The simplest way to ask for things in a shop or at the table: noun + 주세요.

cloze.en: One gimbap, please.

G16.title: "go to (a place)"
G16.expl: 에 marks a destination with verbs like 가다 (go) and 오다 (come).
ex: I'm going to the bank tomorrow.

cloze.en: I'm going to the park.

G17.title: "at, in" (where something happens)
G17.expl: 에서 marks the place where an action happens: 식당에서 먹어요 = I eat at a restaurant. (에 is for where something IS or GOES.)
ex: I buy fruit at the market.

cloze.en: I take a walk in the park.

G18.title: "go (somewhere) to do…"
G18.expl: Verb stem + 러 (after a vowel or ㄹ) / 으러 (after a consonant) + 가요 or 와요: go/come in order to do something.
ex: I'm going to the bookstore to buy a book.

cloze.en: Let's go have coffee. / I'm going for coffee.

G19.title: "and (then)"
G19.expl: Verb stem + 고 links two actions or descriptions: "A and B".
ex: I go to the market and (then) to the bank.
This house is big and quiet.

cloze.en: I eat and then drink coffee.

G20.title: "toward, to (direction)"
G20.expl: (으)로 shows direction: 오른쪽으로 가세요 = go to the right. Use 로 after a vowel or ㄹ, 으로 after other consonants.

cloze.en: Go straight and then go right.

G21.title: past tense
G21.expl: Like the present tense, but add 았/었: 가 → 갔어요, 먹 → 먹었어요, 하 → 했어요.
ex: I went to the market yesterday.

cloze.en: I met a friend yesterday.

G22.title: hours use native numbers, minutes use Sino numbers
G22.expl: Hours: 한 시, 두 시, 세 시, 네 시 … 열두 시. Minutes: 십 분, 삼십 분 (= 반, half). 몇 시예요? = What time is it?
ex: to get up, to wake up

cloze.en: Class starts at nine.

G23.title: "at, on, in" (time)
G23.expl: 에 also marks time: 아침에 (in the morning), 월요일에 (on Monday). Not used with 오늘, 어제, 내일, 지금.
ex: I meet a friend on Saturday.

cloze.en: What do you do on the weekend?

G24.title: "from … to/until"
G24.expl: 부터 = from (a time), 까지 = until / up to. For places, "from" is usually 에서.
ex: 아홉 시부터 한 시까지 수업이 있어요.
I have class from nine to one.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: Until what time do you work?

G25.title: 하나, 둘, 셋 + 개, 명, 살, 병, 잔, 권, 장, 마리
G25.expl: Native numbers count things, people and age. Before a counter, 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네, 스물 → 스무.

cloze.en: One bottle of water, please.

G26.title: "please do … for me"
G26.expl: Verb + 아/어 주세요 asks someone to do something for you. 해 주세요 = please do it.

cloze.en: Please say it once more.

G27.title: prices
G27.expl: 얼마예요? = How much is it? Prices use Sino numbers + 원: 천 원, 만 원, 오천 원.

cloze.en: How much is this umbrella?

G28.title: "only, just"
G28.expl: 만 attaches to a noun and means "only".

cloze.en: I only drink coffee.

G29.title: "can / can't"
G29.expl: Verb stem + ㄹ 수 있어요 (after a vowel) / 을 수 있어요 (after a consonant) = can. 없어요 = can't.
ex: to be (somewhere), there is, to have
to not be, there isn't, to not have

cloze.en: I can do it alone.

G30.title: "can't (unable to)"
G30.expl: 못 before a verb means you're unable to do it (not that you choose not to). 하다 verbs: 공부 못 해요. -지 못해요 is the longer form.

cloze.en: I can't drive.

G31.title: "have to, must"
G31.expl: Verb + 아야/어야 해요 = have to. 해야 해요 = have to do.
ex: I have to get up early.
to get up, to wake up
You have to wash your hands.

cloze.en: You have to wait here.

G32.title: "please don't…"
G32.expl: Verb stem + 지 마세요 = please don't. (From 말다, to stop.)
ex: to stop, to not do (-지 마세요)
to stop, to not do (-지 마세요)

cloze.en: Please don't open the door.

G33.title: "may I…? it's okay to…"
G33.expl: Verb + 아도/어도 돼요 = it's okay to, you may. Ask permission with 돼요?
ex: to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)

cloze.en: Can I eat this?

G34.title: future, "will, going to"
G34.expl: Verb stem + ㄹ 거예요 (after a vowel) / 을 거예요 (after a consonant) talks about plans and guesses about the future.
ex: I'm going to meet a friend on the weekend.

cloze.en: What are you going to do tomorrow?

G35.title: "shall we…? / shall I…?"
G35.expl: Verb stem + ㄹ까요 / 을까요 makes a suggestion or offers help.

cloze.en: What shall we eat?

G36.title: "let's…"
G36.expl: Verb stem + ㅂ시다 / 읍시다 = let's (a bit formal, used in groups). Among friends the plain -아요/어요 form also means "let's": 같이 가요!

cloze.en: Let's go to the park together!

G37.title: "but"
G37.expl: Verb or adjective stem + 지만 joins two contrasting ideas.

cloze.en: It's cold but clear.

G38.title: "Oh, (I see that)…!"
G38.expl: Stem + 네요 shows surprise or a reaction to something you just noticed.
ex: Wow, the view is really beautiful!

cloze.en: This tteokbokki is delicious!

G39.title: "by, with, using"
G39.expl: (으)로 also means "by" or "with": 지하철로 가요 = I go by subway.

cloze.en: I go to school by subway.

G40.title: "and then (go/sit/meet and…)"
G40.expl: Verb + 아서/어서 links two actions where the first sets up the second: 가서 먹어요 = go (there) and eat.
ex: I went to the market and bought fruit.

cloze.en: I met a friend and (we) saw a movie.

G41.title: "it takes (time)"
G41.expl: 얼마나 걸려요? = How long does it take? Answer with a time + 걸려요.
ex: It takes 30 minutes from home to school.
How long does it take to Seoul Station?

cloze.en: It takes 20 minutes by subway.

G42.title: "if, when"
G42.expl: Verb or adjective stem + 면 (after a vowel or ㄹ) / 으면 (after a consonant) = if.
ex: If it rains, I'll stay home.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: If you have time, let's go together.

G43.title: "because, so"
G43.expl: Verb or adjective + 아서/어서 also gives a reason: 아파서 못 가요 = I'm sick so I can't go. (Don't use it with "let's" or "please".)
ex: I had a headache, so I took medicine.

cloze.en: I was hungry, so I ate ramen.

G44.title: "because, since" (with requests)
G44.expl: Stem + 니까 / 으니까 gives a reason, and unlike -아서 it can come before "please" or "let's".
ex: It's raining, so take an umbrella.

cloze.en: It's cold, so dress warmly.

G45.title: 춥다 → 추워요, 듣다 → 들어요, 아프다 → 아파요
G45.expl: Some stems change: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel (춥다 → 추워요, 맵다 → 매워요). ㄷ becomes ㄹ (듣다 → 들어요, 걷다 → 걸어요). ㅡ drops (아프다 → 아파요, 바쁘다 → 바빠요, 크다 → 커요).

cloze.en: The kimchi is too spicy.

G46.title: "…, right?"
G46.expl: Stem + 지요 (often shortened to 죠) asks for agreement or softens a statement.
ex: to be okay, to be fine

cloze.en: Korean is hard, isn't it?

G47.title: "is …-ing" (progressive)
G47.expl: Verb stem + 고 있어요 = doing right now (or these days).
ex: to be (somewhere), there is, to have
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: Grandma is cooking.

G48.title: "…-ing" (turns a verb into a noun)
G48.expl: Verb stem + 는 것 makes "the act of doing": 그림 그리는 것 = drawing. 것 is often said 거 in speech.

cloze.en: Do you like watching movies?

G49.title: "than", "the most"
G49.expl: 보다 means "than": 커피보다 차가 좋아요 = I like tea more than coffee. 제일 or 가장 = the most.
ex: What food do you like the most?

cloze.en: I like baseball more than soccer.

G50.title: "have (ever) done…"
G50.expl: Verb stem + ㄴ/은 적이 있어요 = I have done it before. 없어요 = I never have.
ex: Have you ever seen a Korean movie?
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
to not be, there isn't, to not have

cloze.en: I've made kimchi before.

G51.title: "before …-ing / after …-ing"
G51.expl: Verb stem + 기 전에 = before doing. Verb stem + ㄴ/은 후에 = after doing.
ex: I read before going to sleep.
I take a walk after eating.
a walk, stroll (산책하다 = take a walk)

cloze.en: Wash your hands before eating.

G52.title: describing nouns: "a big house"
G52.expl: To put an adjective before a noun, use stem + ㄴ (after a vowel) / 은 (after a consonant): 크다 → 큰 집, 작다 → 작은 방. 있다/없다 adjectives take 는: 재미있는 영화.
ex: to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: I like quiet places.

G53.title: "the person who…, the thing that…"
G53.expl: A verb stem + 는 describes a noun with an action happening now: 자는 사람 = the person who is sleeping.
ex: Who is the person standing over there?
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
The food I like is bulgogi.

cloze.en: The person drinking coffee is Min-jun.

G54.title: "try (doing)…"
G54.expl: Verb + 아/어 보세요 = try it. Past: 아/어 봤어요 = I tried it.

cloze.en: Try this rice cake.

G55.title: "when…"
G55.expl: Stem + ㄹ 때 / 을 때 = at the time when. With past: -았/었을 때.
ex: When it rains, I use an umbrella.
When I was young, I lived in Busan.

cloze.en: Call me when you have time.

G56.title: showing respect to the person you talk about
G56.expl: Add 시 / 으시 to a verb to show respect for its subject (older people, customers, teachers): 가세요 (she goes), 가셨어요 (she went). Use it for grandma, never for yourself.
ex: The boss is busy right now.

cloze.en: Grandma is reading a book.

G57.title: 드시다, 계시다, 주무시다, 말씀하시다, 댁, 성함, 연세
G57.expl: Some words change completely for respect: 먹다 → 드시다/잡수시다 (eat), 있다 → 계시다 (be somewhere), 자다 → 주무시다 (sleep), 말하다 → 말씀하시다, 집 → 댁, 이름 → 성함, 나이 → 연세.

cloze.en: The boss is in the office now.

G58.title: honorific "to" and subject marker
G58.expl: 께 = to (someone you respect), replacing 에게/한테. 께서 = honorific subject marker, replacing 이/가.
ex: to make, to cook (rice), to build

cloze.en: I asked the teacher a question.

G59.title: "I'll (do it)" — a promise or offer
G59.expl: Verb stem + ㄹ게요 / 을게요 = I'll do it (for you / I promise). Only for your own actions.

cloze.en: I'll do the dishes.

G60.title: "I'll do … for you" (polite)
G60.expl: Verb + 아/어 드릴게요 offers to do something for someone you respect (드리다 is the humble form of 주다).
ex: Shall I take a picture for you?

cloze.en: Grandma, I'll carry your bag for you.

G61.title: "the … that I did"
G61.expl: Verb stem + ㄴ / 은 describes a noun with a past action: 어제 본 영화 = the movie I saw yesterday.
ex: It's the clothes I bought yesterday.

cloze.en: Who is the person you met last week?

G62.title: background, soft "but…", "so…"
G62.expl: -는데 sets up background before the main point, or softens a sentence. Use -는데 with verbs and 있다/없다, -(으)ㄴ데 with adjectives.
ex: It's raining now — do you have an umbrella?
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
It's nice, but a bit expensive.
to be good, to be nice

cloze.en: I'm hungry — shall we eat something?

G63.title: "will (probably), must be", polite set phrases
G63.expl: -겠- guesses ("that must be…") or states intention. You'll hear it in set phrases: 잘 먹겠습니다 (thanks for the food), 알겠습니다 (understood), 모르겠어요 (I'm not sure).

cloze.en: It'll probably be cold tomorrow.

G64.title: formal speech: news, announcements, staff
G64.expl: Formal endings: -ㅂ니다 / -습니다 for statements, -ㅂ니까 / -습니까 for questions. You'll hear them in the subway, on the news and from shop staff.

cloze.en: Nice to meet you (formal).

G65.title: 그리고, 그래서, 그런데, 그러니까, 하지만
G65.expl: Start a sentence with these to connect it to the last one: 그리고 (and), 그래서 (so), 그런데 / 근데 (but, by the way), 하지만 (however), 그러니까 (so, that's why).
ex: It rained. So I stayed home.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
I'm tired. But I can't sleep.

cloze.en: I was hungry. So I ate ramen.

G66.title: casual speech (present & past)
G66.expl: 반말 (casual speech) is polite speech minus 요: 가요 → 가, 먹어요 → 먹어, 했어요 → 했어. Use it with close friends, younger people and kids — only after you've agreed to "drop formalities" (말을 놓다).
ex: What are you doing? Did you eat?

cloze.en: Did you see the movie yesterday?

G67.title: casual "is / isn't"
G67.expl: In 반말, 이에요/예요 becomes 이야 (after a consonant) / 야 (after a vowel), and 아니에요 becomes 아니야. "I" becomes 나 (내가), "you" becomes 너 (네가).

cloze.en: This is my house.

G68.title: "let's" (casual)
G68.expl: Verb stem + 자 = let's, among friends. 같이 가자! = Let's go together!

cloze.en: Let's rest at home today.

G69.title: casual questions
G69.expl: Friends usually just raise the tone of 반말: 밥 먹었어? You'll also hear -니? (soft, often from older people to younger) and -냐? (blunt, between close friends). -(으)ㄹ래? = "want to…?"
ex: Ji-woo, did you do your homework?

cloze.en: Want to go together tomorrow?

G70.title: do something in advance, leave it done
G70.expl: Verb + 아/어 놓다 (or 두다) = do it and leave it that way, ready for later.
ex: I made side dishes for tomorrow.

cloze.en: I left the light on.

G71.title: is (in a state)
G71.expl: Verb + 아/어 있다 describes a state that continues after an action: 앉아 있어요 (is seated), 문이 열려 있어요 (the door is open).
ex: Grandma is sitting on the sofa.
There's a letter lying on the desk.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: The door is open.

G72.title: do completely (often with regret or relief)
G72.expl: Verb + 아/어 버리다 = do it completely, often with a feeling: "ended up…", "went ahead and…".
ex: I ended up eating the whole cake.
to throw away; (-아 버리다 = end up doing)
I got the homework all done!
to throw away; (-아 버리다 = end up doing)

cloze.en: The bus has already left.

G73.title: "after (doing)…, then"
G73.expl: Verb stem + 고 나서 = after finishing one action, then another.
ex: to come out, to occur (열이 나다 = have a fever)
After eating, I did the dishes.
to come out, to occur (열이 나다 = have a fever)

cloze.en: Slice the onion, then stir-fry it.

G74.title: "while (doing)"
G74.expl: Verb stem + 면서 / 으면서 = doing two things at the same time.
ex: I cook while listening to music.

cloze.en: I eat while watching TV.

G75.title: "was doing…, and then (switched)"
G75.expl: Verb stem + 다가 = while doing one thing, you stopped or something else happened.
ex: I was cooking, then took a call.
On my way home, I stopped by the market.
to stop by, to drop in

cloze.en: I fell asleep while studying.

G76.title: "it seems, I think"
G76.expl: Verb + 는 것 같다 (now), -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 (past or adjectives) softens what you say: "I think…", "it seems…".
ex: 이 옷이 좀 큰 것 같아요.
I think this is a bit big.

cloze.ko: 서연 씨가 화가 난 것 같아요.
cloze.en: I think Seo-yeon is upset.

G77.title: "look (adjective)"
G77.expl: Adjective + 아/어 보이다 = to look a certain way.
ex: You look young in those clothes.

cloze.en: This cake looks delicious.

G78.title: "I think it will…, looks like it's going to…"
G78.expl: Stem + ㄹ/을 것 같다 = a guess about the future, or a soft way to say how you feel.
ex: I'm so hungry I could die.
to die (-아 죽겠다 = so … I could die)

cloze.ko: 이 옷은 저한테 작을 것 같아요.
cloze.en: I think this will be too small for me.

G79.title: "you'd better…, it would be good to…"
G79.expl: Verb + 는 게 좋겠어요 gives gentle advice.
ex: You'd better rest at home today.
to be good, to be nice
It'd be good to see a doctor.
to be good, to be nice

cloze.en: You'd better take some medicine.

G80.title: "don't have to"
G80.expl: Verb + 지 않아도 돼요 (or 안 + 아/어도 돼요) = you don't have to.
ex: You don't have to come early tomorrow.
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)

cloze.en: You don't have to go to the hospital today.

G81.title: "it's been (time) since"
G81.expl: Verb + ㄴ/은 지 + time + 됐어요 = it's been … since.
ex: 한국에 온 지 육 개월 됐어요.
It's been six months since I came to Korea.
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)
밥을 먹은 지 두 시간 됐어요.
It's been two hours since I ate.
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)

cloze.ko: 별이가 떠난 지 일 년이 됐어요.
cloze.en: It's been a year since Byeol left.

G82.title: "decide to, plan to"
G82.expl: Verb + 기로 했어요 = decided / agreed to.
ex: I've decided to exercise starting tomorrow.

cloze.en: I decided to memorize words every day.

G83.title: "if you want to, in order to"
G83.expl: Verb + 려면 / 으려면 = if you intend to…
ex: To pass the exam, you have to study hard.
Where do I get off to go to Gyeongbokgung?
to get off, to get out

cloze.en: If you want to be good at Korean, practice every day.

G84.title: "so that, until"
G84.expl: Verb + 도록 = so that (something happens), or until.
ex: I took a note so I wouldn't forget.
note, memo (메모하다 = to take a note)
I studied until late at night.
to be late at night (밤늦게 = late at night)

cloze.en: Be careful not to catch a cold.

G85.title: "come to, end up"
G85.expl: Verb + 게 되다 = something comes about (often not by your own plan).
ex: I ended up living in Seoul because of work.
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)
I've come to like Korean food.
to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)

cloze.en: We're going to work together from next month.

G86.title: "become (adjective)"
G86.expl: Adjective + 아/어지다 = to become: 추워지다 (get cold), 좋아지다 (get better).
ex: to be good, to be nice

cloze.en: I've gotten really busy lately.

G87.title: "know how to"
G87.expl: Verb + ㄹ/을 줄 알아요 = know how to; 몰라요 = don't know how to.
ex: Do you know how to drive?
I don't know how to swim.

cloze.en: I know how to make kimchi.

G88.title: "you know…, as you know"
G88.expl: Stem + 잖아요 reminds the listener of something they already know, sometimes with a little blame.

cloze.en: We ate together yesterday, remember?

G89.title: "you see, (because)…"
G89.expl: Stem + 거든요 explains the background or reason behind what you said.
ex: I can't go today. I have plans, you see.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have
I'm hungry. I skipped breakfast, you see.

cloze.en: I'm tired. I went to bed late, you see.

G90.title: "tend to, be on the … side"
G90.expl: Verb + 는 편이에요 / adjective + (으)ㄴ 편이에요 softens a description: "kind of, rather".
ex: I tend to get up early.
to get up, to wake up
Seo-yeon is on the quiet side.

cloze.en: Min-jun tends to eat a lot.

G91.title: "worried that, in case"
G91.expl: Stem + ㄹ까 봐 / 을까 봐 = because you're worried something might happen.
ex: I took a taxi in case I'd be late.
서연 씨가 싫어할까 봐 말을 못 했어요.
I couldn't say it in case Seo-yeon didn't like it.

cloze.en: I brought an umbrella in case it rains.

G92.title: "I want to / do you want to?"
G92.expl: Verb + ㄹ래요 / 을래요 asks or tells what someone wants to do, in a friendly way.
ex: What would you like to drink?
I think I'll just stay home.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: Want to watch a movie?

G93.title: "almost (happened)"
G93.expl: Verb + ㄹ/을 뻔했어요 = something almost happened (but didn't).
ex: I overslept and was almost late.

cloze.en: I almost missed the bus.

G94.title: "whether, what/where/how…"
G94.expl: Verb + 는지 (adjectives -(으)ㄴ지) turns a question into part of a sentence: 어디 있는지 알아요? (Do you know where it is?)
ex: Do you know where Byeol lives?
I don't know how much this is.

cloze.en: I don't know who that person is.

G95.title: "whether (it will)…"
G95.expl: Stem + ㄹ지 / 을지 talks about uncertain future things: 올지 안 올지 = whether or not she'll come.
ex: I don't know if it'll rain tomorrow.
Have you decided what to eat?

cloze.en: I'm not sure whether Byeol will reply.

G96.title: "it seems (from what I see)"
G96.expl: Verb + 나 보다 / adjective + (으)ㄴ가 보다 = guessing from evidence: 비가 오나 봐요 (It must be raining — people have umbrellas).
ex: It looks like it's snowing outside.

cloze.en: Grandma must be sleeping.

G97.title: very polite request
G97.expl: Verb + 아/어 주시겠어요? is a very polite "Would you please…?" — good for banks, offices and strangers.
ex: Would you write your name here, please?
Could you wait a moment, please?

cloze.en: Could you say that again, please?

G98.title: "since I'll…, so you…"
G98.expl: Stem + ㄹ/을 테니까 = since (I'll do / it will be) X, (you do) Y.
ex: It'll be cold, so dress warmly.

cloze.en: I'll wait, so take your time.

G99.pattern: Passive verbs: 보이다, 들리다, 열리다, 닫히다
G99.title: "is seen, is heard, opens"
G99.expl: Some verbs have passive forms with 이/히/리/기: 보다 → 보이다 (be seen), 듣다 → 들리다 (be heard), 열다 → 열리다 (open by itself), 닫다 → 닫히다 (close by itself).
ex: You can see the sea from here.
to close (by itself), to be shut

cloze.en: I can hear a strange sound.

G100.title: reported statements: "(someone) says that…"
G100.expl: Statement + 다고 하다 reports what someone said: 간다고 했어요 (said they'd go). Verbs: -ㄴ/는다고, adjectives: -다고, nouns: -(이)라고.
ex: Grandma said it will rain tomorrow.

cloze.en: Seo-yeon said she'd be late.

G101.title: reported questions
G101.expl: Question + 냐고 (or -느냐고) 하다/묻다 reports a question: 어디 가냐고 물었어요 (asked where I'm going).
ex: Ji-woo asked how old I am.
도윤 씨가 별 씨를 아냐고 물어봤어요.
Do-yoon asked if I know Byeol.

cloze.en: Grandma asked if I'd eaten.

G102.title: reported suggestions and commands
G102.expl: Suggestion + 자고 하다: 같이 가자고 했어요 (suggested going together). Command + (으)라고 하다: 쉬라고 했어요 (told me to rest).
ex: 민준 씨가 같이 여행 가자고 했어요.
The doctor told me to rest well.

cloze.en: Grandma told me to go to bed early.

G103.title: "they say…" (contractions)
G103.expl: In speech, -다고 해요 shortens to -대요, and -(이)라고 해요 to -래요. Very common in gossip and news-telling.
ex: They say Do-yoon is a game-company CEO!

cloze.en: They say that restaurant is good.

G104.title: "that used to…, that I was (doing)"
G104.expl: Verb + 던 + noun recalls something repeated or unfinished in the past: 내가 다니던 학교 (the school I used to attend).
ex: These are clothes Grandma used to wear when she was young.
Where's the bread I was eating earlier?
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: It's the neighborhood I used to live in.

G105.title: "I noticed / I found that…"
G105.expl: Stem + 더라고요 shares something you saw or experienced yourself: 바다가 정말 예쁘더라고요 (The sea was really beautiful — I saw it).
ex: 강릉에 가 보니까 바다가 정말 맑더라고요.
When I went to Gangneung, the sea was really clear.
He sings really well, I noticed.

cloze.en: The coffee at that café was good, I found.

G106.title: "that (once) was / had done"
G106.expl: Verb + 았/었던 + noun points to a completed past experience: 작년에 갔던 곳 (the place I went last year).
ex: This is the café Byeol used to come to.
It's a song I loved as a kid.

cloze.en: Do you remember the day we first met?

G107.title: "worth (doing)"
G107.expl: Verb + ㄹ/을 만해요 = worth doing; good enough.
ex: This movie is really worth watching.
to hold in, to put up with

cloze.en: Gangneung is worth visiting once.

G108.title: "and so, because" (spoken)
G108.expl: In casual speech, -아/어 가지고 often replaces -아/어서: "so", "and then".
ex: I was so tired, so I went to bed early.
to have, to take (가지고 오다 = bring)
I bought it at the market and brought it.
to have, to take (가지고 오다 = bring)

cloze.en: I lost my wallet, so I went to the police station.

G109.title: "because (unexpectedly)…" (usually bad results)
G109.expl: Verb + 는 바람에 = because of something unexpected, usually with a bad result.
ex: I overslept, so I missed the bus.
to miss (a bus, a chance), to let go
갑자기 비가 오는 바람에 옷이 다 젖었어요.
It suddenly rained, so my clothes got soaked.

cloze.en: I was late because of the traffic.

G110.title: "even if, even though"
G110.expl: Stem + 아/어도 = even if: 비가 와도 가요 (I'll go even if it rains).
ex: No matter how much I look, it's not there.
to not be, there isn't, to not have
Even if you're busy, you have to eat.

cloze.en: I'll go even if it rains.

G111.title: "I heard that…, is it true?"
G111.expl: Statement + 다면서요? checks something you heard: 이사한다면서요? (I heard you're moving — right?)
ex: I hear Do-yoon's company is famous — is that right?
I heard you're going on a trip next month?

cloze.en: I heard Min-jun passed the exam?

G112.title: "I can't believe that…!"
G112.expl: Statement + 다니 expresses surprise at news: 벌써 겨울이라니! (It's already winter? Unbelievable!)
ex: older brother (said by a girl or woman)
to be like this (이렇게 = like this)

cloze.en: It's already midnight?!

G113.title: "at least, even (if just)"
G113.expl: Noun + (이)라도 = "if not the best option, at least…": 커피라도 마실래요? (Want at least a coffee?)
ex: If you're busy, at least give me a call.

cloze.en: Let's meet on the weekend, even just briefly.

G114.title: "in order to"
G114.expl: Verb + 기 위해서 = in order to (a bit formal; in speech also -(으)려고).
ex: I walk every day for my health.
to be for, for the sake of
I came to Korea to learn Korean.
to be for, for the sake of

cloze.en: I got up early to help Grandma.

G115.title: "while, during the time that"
G115.expl: Verb + 는 동안 = during the time something happens.
ex: 제가 요리하는 동안 상을 차려 주세요.
Please set the table while I cook.
to set (a table), to prepare (a meal)
I learned a lot while I was in Korea.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: Be quiet while Grandma is sleeping.

G116.title: "make / let someone do"
G116.expl: Verb + 게 하다 = make or let someone do something.
ex: Grandma made us go to bed early.

cloze.en: My mom made me eat it.

G117.title: "used to (often)"
G117.expl: Verb + 곤 하다 = something you did regularly, often in the past.
ex: As a child I'd often play at the sea.
Grandpa used to sing in the evenings.

cloze.en: I used to go hiking every weekend.

G118.title: "had done (but no longer)"
G118.expl: Double past -았/었었- describes something that was true in the past but has changed.
ex: This house used to have many students.
to be many, to be a lot
Byeol had lived in this room.

cloze.en: I used to smoke (but I quit).

G119.title: "as it is, while still…"
G119.expl: Verb + ㄴ/은 채로 = in the state of having done it: 신발을 신은 채로 (with your shoes still on).
ex: I fell asleep with the light on.
Don't come in with your shoes on.
to stop, to not do (-지 마세요)

cloze.en: I went out with the window open.

G120.title: "as soon as"
ex: I went to sleep as soon as I got home.
We took photos as soon as we reached the top.

cloze.en: I went home as soon as class ended.

G121.title: "the more…, the more…"
G121.expl: Stem + ㄹ/을수록 = the more. Often with 하면 할수록 (the more you do it).
ex: The more I learn Korean, the more fun it is.
The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

cloze.en: The more I listen to this song, the more I like it.

G122.title: "because I was busy (doing)…"
G122.expl: Verb + 느라고 = because you were doing something (so you couldn't do another thing).
ex: I couldn't answer because I was studying.
Climbing the mountain wore me out.

cloze.en: I was working, so I couldn't eat.

G123.title: "according to"
G123.expl: Noun + 에 따르면 = according to (news, reports).
ex: 뉴스에 따르면 내일 눈이 온다고 합니다.
According to the news, it will snow tomorrow.
조사에 따르면 청소년의 독서 시간이 줄었습니다.
According to a survey, teens' reading time has decreased.

cloze.en: According to the forecast, it will be clear.

G124.title: "whereas, on the other hand"
G124.expl: Stem + 는 반면에 (adjectives -(으)ㄴ 반면에) contrasts two facts.
ex: Seoul is convenient, but on the other hand it's too crowded.

cloze.ko: 이 집은 넓은 반면에 좀 어두워요.
cloze.en: This house is spacious but a bit dark.

G125.title: "because" (formal, clear reason)
G125.expl: Stem + 기 때문에 gives a clear, often formal reason; N 때문에 = because of N.
ex: 길이 막히기 때문에 지하철을 타는 게 좋겠습니다.
Because traffic is heavy, it's better to take the subway.
to be good, to be nice
People are worried because of environmental problems.

cloze.en: Because it's cold, watch out for colds.

G126.title: "so much that, to the point of"
G126.expl: Stem + ㄹ/을 정도로 = to such a degree that…
ex: I laughed so hard I cried.
to come out, to occur (열이 나다 = have a fever)
집값이 믿을 수 없을 정도로 올랐어요.
Housing prices rose to an unbelievable degree.
to not be, there isn't, to not have

cloze.en: I ate so much my stomach hurt.

G127.title: "instead of; in exchange for"
G127.expl: Verb + 는 대신에 = instead of doing / in return for doing.
ex: Instead of taking a taxi, I walked.
to walk (somewhere), to go on foot
제가 요리하는 대신에 설거지는 네가 해.
I'll cook, and in exchange you do the dishes.

cloze.en: I drink tea instead of coffee.

G128.title: "as much as"
G128.expl: Noun + 만큼 = as much as, to the same degree as.
ex: 민준 씨만큼 요리를 잘하는 사람은 없어요.
No one cooks as well as Min-jun.
to not be, there isn't, to not have
It's not as expensive as I thought.

cloze.ko: 저도 할머니만큼 김치를 잘 만들고 싶어요.
cloze.en: I want to make kimchi as well as Grandma.

G129.title: "have no choice but to"
G129.expl: Verb + ㄹ/을 수밖에 없다 = can only, have no choice but to.
ex: There was no bus, so I had no choice but to walk.
to not be, there isn't, to not have
to walk (somewhere), to go on foot
to not be, there isn't, to not have
이 웹툰은 인기가 많을 수밖에 없어요.
This webtoon can't help but be popular.
to be many, to be a lot
to not be, there isn't, to not have

cloze.en: I had no money, so I had to give up.

G130.title: "only, just (keep doing)"
G130.expl: Verb + 기만 하다 = only/just do that and nothing else.
ex: My little brother does nothing but play games all day.
to stop, to not do (-지 마세요)

cloze.en: Seo-yeon just keeps drawing.

G131.title: "even (surprisingly, negatively)"
G131.expl: Noun + 조차 or 마저 = even (in a negative or extreme situation): 이름조차 몰라요 (I don't even know the name).
ex: I was so busy I couldn't even eat.
to throw away; (-아 버리다 = end up doing)

cloze.en: I don't even know that person's name.

G132.title: "there's no way that…"
G132.expl: Stem + ㄹ/을 리가 없다 = it can't be true that…
ex: There's no way Ji-woo would lie.
reason, way (-ㄹ 리가 없다 = there's no way)
to not be, there isn't, to not have
그 그림이 미래를 알 리가 없잖아요.
That drawing can't possibly know the future.
reason, way (-ㄹ 리가 없다 = there's no way)
to not be, there isn't, to not have

cloze.en: There's no way Grandma doesn't know.

G133.title: "if (only) I had…"
G133.expl: Verb + 았/었더라면 = if (something had happened in the past), often with regret.
ex: It would've been good if I'd said it earlier.
to be good, to be nice
If I'd called then, we could have met.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: If only I'd come a little earlier.

G134.title: "pretend to"
ex: Ji-woo pretended not to know anything.
to stop, to not do (-지 마세요)

cloze.en: Min-jun pretended he was okay.

G135.title: "I should have…"
G135.expl: Verb + ㄹ/을걸 (그랬다) expresses regret: "I should have…"
ex: I should have brought an umbrella.

cloze.en: I should have said it honestly back then.

G136.title: "I've got to…; you should…"
G136.expl: Verb + 아/어야지 = a resolution ("I'd better…") or advice/scolding to someone close.
ex: I really need to study now.
If you're sick, you should go to the hospital!

cloze.en: I've got to start exercising tomorrow.

G137.title: "either…or; whatever"
G137.expl: Stem + 든지 lists options or means "no matter what": 가든지 말든지 (go or don't, whatever).
ex: to be good, to be nice
Whatever happens, I believe in you.
to be (somewhere), there is, to have

cloze.en: Come or don't — do as you like.

G138.title: "hope that"
G138.expl: Verb + 기를 바라요 = I hope that…

cloze.en: I hope you pass the exam.

G139.title: "I wish, it would be nice if"
G139.expl: Stem + (으)면 좋겠어요 = I wish / I hope.
ex: I wish the first snow would come.
the first snow of the year
to be good, to be nice
I wish Byeol would come back.
to be good, to be nice

cloze.en: I hope it's clear tomorrow.

G140.title: "while you're at it"
G140.expl: Verb + 는 김에 (past -(으)ㄴ 김에) = since you're already doing X, also do Y.
ex: 시장에 가는 김에 우유도 사 올게요.
Since I'm going to the market, I'll get milk too.
Since we're on the subject, let me ask you something.

cloze.en: While I was in Seoul, I met a friend.

G141.title: "not only…but also"
G141.expl: Stem + ㄹ/을 뿐만 아니라 = not only…, but also. Noun + 뿐만 아니라.
ex: 할머니는 요리를 잘할 뿐만 아니라 노래도 잘하세요.
Grandma not only cooks well but sings well too.
이 집은 따뜻할 뿐만 아니라 사람들도 따뜻해요.
This house is not only warm — the people are warm too.

cloze.en: Korean is not only fun but also useful.

G142.title: "start (doing)"
G142.expl: Verb + 기 시작하다 = to begin doing.
ex: to get off, to get out
I started learning Korean last year.

cloze.ko: 서연 씨가 새 웹툰을 그리기 시작했어요.
cloze.en: Seo-yeon started drawing a new webtoon.
